Q: Some questions about ARM/ARM64 write combine(NORMAL_NC) memory attribute read/write and memory barriers A:

I had to Google so much to solve this

Your first guess is correct, because ARM64 allows aggresive execution and out of order execution, the CPU pipeline can preform a route the value of val straight to the destination register of the return statement without doing a read write transfer on the DDR bus. Without barriers, you are testing CPU register/buffer tracking, not what you want. Your second guess is sort of correct, dsb sy will halt CPU execution until the write buffer is drained and the write request is acknowledged. But a barrier after the write will not make it so the earlyer read instruction won't be executed speculatively or read out of peripheral path.

Take everything I said with a grain of rice, I am not an expert at thid.

Q: Are these colours blended correctly? A:

So a year later I've come back to this. The problem is almost certainly doing blending in non-linear space. The transition between red (1.0, 0, 0) and green (0, 1.0, 0) meets up at about (0.5, 0.5, 0), which, kind of sounds right, but isn't the right way to do blending in this setting. GIMP is linearising the colour values, interpolating, and converting back to non-linear sRGB, and the value in between the green and red is about ( 0.74, 0.74, 0), close to the sRGB value of 0.732 for linear 0.5. 0.5 intensity isn't strong enough for our vision, it should be higher, in the seventies, and why the first one looks wrong but the second one looks right. Colour should always (almost) be blended in linear space for reasons like this.
